correctness.rationale: An edge-length-l regular simplex is isometric to a coordinate simplex scaled by l/sqrt(2). The exact distance to the k-composition grid reduces to integer rounding of q=kp. An integer exchange argument establishes floor/ceiling rounding with r integer increments, and the hypersimplex decomposition bounds the squared nearest error by r-sum(f_i^2), at most r(d-r)/d, with equality if and only if all fractional coordinates equal r/d. Every feasible r is realized, so maximizing r(d-r) gives the claimed all-dimensional formula and completely classifies the equality points. Stars-and-bars gives the exact cardinality. The independent checker enumerates small dimensions and k but is explicitly not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The distance from finite Minkowski averages to a convex hull is the exact natural invariant studied in recent convexification work. On its canonical regular-simplex vertex example, the full dimension-by-averaging index profile is unknown from the inspected sources and includes a meaningful boundary phenomenon: the centroid alone is the worst point through a dimension-dependent cutoff, after which a combinatorially classifiable family of deep holes appears. The exact all-k sharp radius, complete maximizer classification, and explicit counts reveal precisely when the finite nonnegative boundary stops lowering the familiar root-lattice covering radius. This is a motivated natural complete classification, not a standalone arbitrary numerical slice; no general theorem-sized downstream application is falsely claimed.
